Lee Strobel was an atheist legal journalist who set out to disprove Christianity and ended up a pastor and bestselling author. With Tucker Carlson, he discusses the subjects of his later books: demonic possession, miracles, visions, and encounters with angels and demons reported by people he interviewed.

Strobel presents cases the way he once presented evidence, witness by witness. Carlson, who speaks often about spiritual forces in public life, meets him on that ground gladly. Skeptics will want more than testimony, and the episode does not pretend to laboratory proof. What it offers is a trained investigator's case that the supernatural is real and active, argued to an audience Carlson has primed to take the question seriously.
podcast-dannyjones-7ymTSiml8W8:
Nathan Apffel, a filmmaker, joins Danny Jones to argue that the Vatican is covering up what he calls the most evil crime in history. His case, built through his documentary work, accuses the Church's highest levels of hiding abuse and worse, protected by centuries of institutional secrecy.

Apffel lays out his evidence and his theory of why the truth stays buried. Jones tests the chain of claims, which reach far beyond the documented abuse scandals into territory listeners will find hard to credit. The accusations are Apffel's, presented as he makes them, and they remain unproven. The episode is preserved as an artifact of a genre: the total-cover-up argument, delivered by a committed advocate to an audience that rewards exactly this kind of certainty.
podcast-joerogan-se8WZSPujW8:
Eddie Bravo shares his take on recent UFO news in this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Bravo, a jiu-jitsu coach and comic, is Rogan's oldest friend on the show and its most famous conspiracy voice. His catchphrase advice to look into it sums up his whole approach.

Bravo reacts to the latest sightings and official statements with cheerful suspicion. He questions every simple answer and floats wilder ones of his own. Rogan teases him while still enjoying the ride, as longtime listeners expect. The segment is less a briefing than a hangout with the show's beloved wild card.
